requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only. It has no load or strength rating, so the 50 kg capacity can't be verified or claimed. That depends on the print material and settings, and on load testing.

finish.summary:
I built a small shelf unit with two drawers. It can't be rated for 50 kg: the configurator only checks that parts fit and don't collide, and knows nothing about strength or loads.

The unit is two storeys high. Each storey has a full hex base in the middle with a south-half base on each side. The two lower half bases each hold a drawer. The open faces are capped with solid end caps and the joints are bolted. Three covers make a flat top shelf 160 mm off the bench, and I put a row of books on it to show it in use. A stack of books and a single book didn't fit beside the row on the narrow top, so I left them off.

The build check passed with no issues and the mesh-collision check reads clear. It comes to 53 parts, about 2,527 g of filament and roughly 3,761 minutes (about 63 hours) of printing. Before trusting it with a heavy load of books, you'd need to load-test the printed parts in your chosen material.

M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
